newsitem.title: UK: Baltic Exchange seeks finance chief.
newsitem.headline: Baltic Exchange seeks finance chief.

text.p: The world's oldest shipping market the Baltic Exchange advertised Thursday for a head of finance - possibly the first in its 253 year history.
The Baltic said it is seeking a head of finance to help formulate a business plan and take full responsibility for managing all aspects of finance, membership and administration of the exchange.
The move comes amid steps being taken by the dry bulk shipping exchange to simplify its arcane membership system and introduce a new corporate structure.

The Baltic Exchange has undergone a turbulent period since being bombed out of its old site by the IRA in 1992. It has also suffered from changing business patterns as the use of modern communications have left its 4,000 sq ft trading floor deserted on most days.
It is currently putting together a new business plan which is aimed at cutting its operating deficit - possibly by letting out its prestigious first floor restaurant for public or corporate use.
Members and shareholders did not express opposition to the proposals floated at its recent annual general meeting.
However, the exchange has been wracked by disagreement over its finances since moving next door to its current smaller site.

The insurance payment on the bombed-out Exchange, which was the subject of now withdrawn planning application by engineering and construction group Kvaerner ASA to build the largest office block in London, released funds which have led to pressure from some shareholders for a special dividend on the 18.5 million sterling which was banked.

Proposals by the Exchange board to change the articles of association were rejected by the AGM a year ago and plans to set a special dividend of 100 stg per share were withdrawn ahead of this year's meeting when it became apparent they would not be passed.
The Baltic's dividend plans were a response to proposals in a business plan compiled by consultants Deloitte & Touche earlier this year to make a 200-250 stg payment.

The Deloitte plan was rejected by the board which considered it unwise to use a large part of its assets before finding a way to replace the investment income. The consultants' plan also envisaged a major reduction in the Baltic's executive structure. -Paul Berrill Reuters Shipping News + 44 171 542 4087. Fax 5017.
